subject.title: Feature: Inter-session progress streaming for sessions_send (ACP/long-running session support)

question: What permanent run-progress observation contract should OpenClaw expose for peer `sessions_send` runs, and what authorization/redaction boundaries must it enforce?
rationale: The implementation shape determines core Gateway RPC/tool surface, event retention, observer authorization, ACP/Codex payload redaction, and channel delivery behavior, which are product and security decisions that source inspection cannot safely choose.

options.title: Design `sessions_subscribe` plus `agent.events`
options.body: Add a separate caller-readable subscription/long-poll surface backed by bounded event buffering and strict session/A2A visibility checks.

options.title: Fold progress into `sessions_send`
options.body: Add an explicit progress mode to `sessions_send`, preserving default compatibility while defining how tool-call responses carry progress and final state.

options.title: Defer to broader process events
options.body: Keep this issue blocked behind the structured process-event contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/52826 and avoid a narrower session-send API for now.

recommendation.title: Design `sessions_subscribe` plus `agent.events`
recommendation.body: Add a separate caller-readable subscription/long-poll surface backed by bounded event buffering and strict session/A2A visibility checks.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest recent cross-cutting history on sessions_send, ACP/session behavior, and gateway API surfaces among the inspected files.
